topics.topic: Whether bubblewrap must preserve and pass the execute_function trap-channel descriptors to the sandbox child
questions: Must bubblewrap preserve these descriptors for the runner, or must the requirement that it has no descriptor-preservation option change?
Must the child receive these descriptors using bubblewrap's --preserve-fds option, or must the requirement that bubblewrap keep them open for the child change?
Which passage must change: must bubblewrap preserve the trap-channel descriptor for the child using its descriptor-preservation option, or is the child not required to inherit it?

quotes: Every descriptor the environment needs from the parent — the write end of the trap channel, the --info-fd pipe — reaches bubblewrap by inheritance, passed with subprocess pass_fds, and bubblewrap keeps it open for the child: bubblewrap has no option that names a descriptor to keep, and --preserve-fds does not exist.
judgement.why: This asks the same question as P1 on the same unchanged passage.

precedent.topic: How bubblewrap preserves the inherited trap-channel descriptor for the runner without a descriptor-preservation option
quotes: Every descriptor the environment needs from the parent — the write end of the trap channel, the --info-fd pipe — reaches bubblewrap by inheritance, passed with subprocess pass_fds, and bubblewrap keeps it open for the child: bubblewrap has no option that names a descriptor to keep, and --preserve-fds does not exist.
precedent.why: The text explicitly requires pass_fds inheritance into bubblewrap and requires bubblewrap to keep the descriptors open for its child.

topics.topic: Whether and how a non-empty mapped node's aggregate value output is persisted when first delivered
questions: Must a non-empty mapped node's aggregate value output be written when first delivered in a separate change with no executions, or must every output be written in the change of the NodeExecution that produces it?

Must a non-empty mapped node's aggregated value output be written in a separate RecordRunProgressChange with no executions when first delivered, or must every output be written in the change of the NodeExecution that produces it?
Is a mapped node's non-empty value list an output derived and stored by runs when first delivered, or does the rule that runs-derived StoredValues are never outputs exclude it?

quotes: A value port's PortRef names exactly one StoredValue; a mapped node's value output, once every element succeeded, is one StoredValue holding the canonical JSON array of the elements' values in element order, whose value_schema is the canonical array schema with the port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items) as items, of the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input, its value_digest is content_identity of a BytesContent holding the bytes and value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent, published with put_value_bytes and written by runs when the list is first delivered, never in an element's own change — except the empty list, which the node's one NodeExecution over an empty list names and writes (A13 rule 6);

Every StoredValue runs derives as an input for delivery — the list element a mapped element receives, and a mapped node's value list when first delivered; never an output, which is written in the change of the NodeExecution that produces it, the [] output of a mapped node over an empty list included — MUST be written with record_change in a RecordRunProgressChange with no executions, status running and the run's waiting points and outputs unchanged before fit_port_value checks it and before execute_function_element or reach_operation_element receives it: read_value_bytes, and every module below runs, reads only a StoredValue that is written.
judgement.divergence: One implementer writes the non-empty mapped aggregate output in a separate RecordRunProgressChange with no executions when it is first delivered; another treats it as an output that must have been written in the producing NodeExecution's change. Downstream nodes, flow-output callers, and the store observe different persistence timing and record contents.
judgement.why: The aggregate is explicitly called a mapped node's value output written by runs on first delivery outside element changes, while another passage says runs-derived delivery values are never outputs and outputs are written with their producing NodeExecution.

topics.topic: Whether input availability alone determines node readiness when mapped elements are waiting
questions: Must readiness depend only on all input ports holding values, or must a node with ready inputs but only waiting elements be classified as not ready?

quotes: A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element that has no concluded record and does not wait — an operation element that waits is not reached again here — before the next node is selected; an operation element waits when operation_element_conclusion answers ElementWaiting, whether or not it has a NodeExecution (one waiting for the owner's approval has none), and a node none of whose elements without a concluded record can execute is not ready, so the next ready node is selected among the others;
judgement.why: The text expressly classifies a node with no executable unconcluded elements as not ready, even if its inputs are present.
